name: Alphabet Inc. (Google LLC)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Google is the hyperscaler most structurally invested in storage-anchored energy: it bought a renewables developer outright (Intersect Power, ~$4.75B — 2.2 GW solar + 2.4 GWh BESS, closed March 2026), anchored the largest battery project ever announced by energy capacity (300 MW / 30 GWh Form Energy iron-air, Minnesota), and signed the largest US solar+storage PPA (Steel River, up to 2.5 GW solar + 2.9 GWh BESS) — while its TPU v7 (Ironwood) became the first credible external threat to NVIDIA (Anthropic up to ~1M TPUs; Meta a multi-billion TPU lessee). BACKGROUND: Founded 1998; Alphabet holding structure since 2015. FY2025 revenue $402.8B (+15%), net income $132.2B; Google Cloud accelerated to +82% in Q2 2026 ($24.8B, backlog $514B); 2026 capex guided $195–205B after three raises; Gemini 3 launched November 2025 (app at 950M MAU); Apple selected Gemini to power the revamped Siri. THE OTHER HALF OF THE BALANCE SHEET — AND THE PART GOOGLE DOES NOT DISCLOSE: since August 2025 Google has been underwriting the rent of a chain of AI data-centre campuses it neither owns nor leases. Under per-building Recognition Agreements it promises the LANDLORD that, on a payment default or insolvency of the tenant — Fluidstack Ltd in every case — it will either pay the termination fee or pay all rent currently due and assume the lease itself. Disclosed support: ~$3.2B at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner, $1.3B at Abernathy, $1.73B at Cipher's Barber Lake, the full 15-year base term of Hut 8's $7.0B River Bend lease, and a master lease at New Lebanon, Indiana. The price varied: penny warrants over ~14% of TeraWulf and ~5.4% of Cipher — and NOTHING AT ALL at Hut 8, where the consideration is instead a springing Alphabet guarantee. THE DISCLOSURE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING: 'Fluidstack' and 'Recognition Agreement' each return ZERO hits across every Alphabet SEC filing indexed by EDGAR full-text search, against 143 corpus-wide hits for 'Fluidstack' — Google has published nothing naming the tenant, and the entire programme is legible only from the landlords' 8-Ks and 10-Qs. Anthropic, an Alphabet investee and Google's largest external TPU customer, is the end user at River Bend.
ecosystemRole: We assess Google as the ecosystem's most storage-forward buyer and its most vertically integrated: the Intersect acquisition brings development in-house ('energy parks' co-locating data centers with behind-the-meter solar+BESS to bypass interconnection queues — first: Haskell County TX, 640 MW solar + 1.3 GWh BESS beside a new campus), 1 GW of data-center demand response is signed across five utilities, and the Form Energy deal legitimizes multi-day (100-hour) storage for AI load. Its 24/7 CFE goal (66% hourly matched; footprint nonetheless +81% vs 2019) is the structural driver of all of it. We further assess the Fluidstack backstop programme as capacity procurement wearing the clothes of credit support: Google obtains first call on gigawatts of AI capacity — at campuses that sometimes run its own silicon for its own investee — without the leases, the land or the project debt touching Alphabet's balance sheet, while the landlords obtain paper financeable at investment grade. The instrument is measured and load-bearing on the other side of the trade: Cipher carries a $544.5M asset for 'the value of Google agreeing to make the lease payments from Fluidstack', and its project notes amortise against the backstop rather than a fixed schedule. Two cautions follow. The equity strip is NEGOTIATED, NOT STRUCTURAL — Hut 8 paid none of it for the largest lease in the set — so the ~14% and ~5.4% taken elsewhere should not be read as the standing price. And the exposure RAMPS WITH DELIVERED CAPACITY, not with announcements: the backstops switch on at lease commencement, which is why TeraWulf recorded only $600M of it becoming effective when CB-3 was delivered. No source publishes a programme-level total, and River Bend's 'full base term' is a description rather than a dollar cap, so the components cannot honestly be summed into one exposure number.

productsAndServices.name: Google Cloud & TPU Silicon
productsAndServices.category: Cloud + custom silicon · the accelerating franchise
productsAndServices.description: Google Cloud: $24.8B in Q2 2026 (+82%, fastest of the big three), $8.8B operating income, backlog $514B (nearly doubled sequentially in Q1). TPU line: v6 Trillium → v7 Ironwood (4.6 PFLOPS FP8/chip, 192 GB HBM3e, 9,216-chip pods at 42.5 exaFLOPS; GA November 2025) — now sold to select external customers rather than cloud-rental only, with Anthropic as anchor (up to ~1M TPUs) and Meta signed as a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar TPU lessee (Feb 2026). Axion Arm CPUs; Gemini 3/3.5 models; DeepMind research arm.
highlights: SemiAnalysis called Ironwood 'the 900lb gorilla' — Google's first credible merchant-silicon threat to NVIDIA; reported (not guided) internal goal of capturing ~10% of NVIDIA-class revenue
Q2 2026 headline EPS $9.11 was almost entirely mark-to-market gains on equity stakes (reported to include Anthropic and SpaceX); ex-gains ~$2.85 — roughly in line
Apple chose Gemini for the revamped Siri (2026) — distribution the antitrust remedies were designed to constrain
Cloud growth outpaced Azure (+40%) and AWS (+28%) in Q1 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The TPU vertical-integration cost edge is the analyst consensus differentiator vs NVIDIA-dependent rivals; the search-antitrust remedies (no Chrome divestiture, but exclusive-deal bans and data-sharing; DOJ cross-appeal pending) are the open regulatory overhang
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cloud consumption; TPU external sales/leases to select customers; ads auction for the core business
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Enterprises, frontier labs (Anthropic), Meta, consumers (Gemini app 950M MAU)
productsAndServices.roadmap: TPU v8 training/inference split ('Sunfish'/'Zebrafish') reported for ~2027 — not company-confirmed; 2027 capex guided to 'significantly increase' again

productsAndServices.name: Energy Parks & Storage Procurement
productsAndServices.category: Power · the most BESS-relevant hyperscaler program
productsAndServices.description: Intersect Power owned outright (~$4.75B; ~2.2 GW solar + 2.4 GWh BESS operating/under construction; energy-park model co-locating DCs with behind-the-meter generation+storage — first park at Haskell County, TX: 640 MW solar + 1.3 GWh BESS). Form Energy iron-air multi-day storage: 300 MW / 30 GWh with Xcel serving the Pine Island, MN data center (largest battery project by energy capacity announced worldwide; Google pays full costs via a new tariff + $50M into Xcel's distributed-battery program). Steel River (Cypress Creek, AR): VPPA for 100% of initial output — phase 1: 1.6 GW solar + ~2 GWh BESS, full build 2.5 GW/2.9 GWh, the largest US solar+storage project to break ground. Texas: 6,200+ MW of PPAs incl. co-located solar+BESS at the Haskell DC. Demand response: 1 GW signed across I&M, TVA, Entergy Arkansas, Minnesota Power, DTE. Nuclear: Kairos master agreement (up to 500 MW; Hermes 2 groundbreaking April 2026, ops ~2030 — nothing flows before ~2030). Fusion: Commonwealth Fusion Systems 200 MW offtake (early 2030s). Hydro: Brookfield framework up to 3 GW (670 MW/$3B+ initial). Geothermal: Fervo EGS operating since 2024.
highlights: The only hyperscaler that owns a major renewables developer — vertical integration into generation+storage development itself
24/7 CFE reality check: 66% hourly matched, 12+ GW contracted in 2025 alone — but total carbon footprint +18% in 2025 and +81% vs 2019; Google concedes the moonshot is 'getting harder'
The Fort Wayne I&M deal (Clean Capacity Arrangement + ML-workload-shifting demand response) is filed as a model tariff structure for AI load
productsAndServices.positioning: Where Amazon buys storage through developer PPAs and Microsoft buys grid firmness, Google builds and owns the storage-anchored infrastructure — the deepest direct BESS demand signal in the covered set
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owned development (Intersect), VPPAs, utility tariffs, DR programs
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Counterparties: utilities (Xcel, TVA, I&M), developers (Cypress Creek), storage innovators (Form Energy, Energy Dome)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Haskell energy park completing ~2026; Steel River phases through decade-end; Hermes 2 ~2030; CFS fusion early 2030s

Funding shifted to capital markets: $24.8B notes (Nov 2025), ~$49.6B equity/convertible raise + $20.3B notes (2026)
AI-search cannibalization is the standing bear question; Google's counter: AI features drive query growth

recentDevelopments.headline: Fluidstack — the tenant Google's whole backstop programme stands behind — valued at USD 18B, explicitly on the strength of building Google's and Anthropic's data centres
recentDevelopments.read: The backstop is doing double duty: it de-risks the landlords' paper AND capitalises the tenant. Google has never named Fluidstack publicly, yet the market prices Fluidstack largely on that relationship.

recentDevelopments.headline: USD 600M of Google's TeraWulf support became effective on CB-3 delivery — the backstops switch on at lease commencement, not at signing
recentDevelopments.read: The programme's exposure ramps with delivered capacity rather than with announcements, so the headline backstop totals overstate what is live at any date. Track energisation, not signings.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: revenue $119.8B (+24%) beat; Cloud +82%; capex raised a third time to $195–205B — stock fell up to ~7%
recentDevelopments.read: The Alphabet version of the sector pattern: fundamentals beat, capex shocks — with the added wrinkle that headline EPS was mostly unrealized equity gains (composition disputed across outlets; verify in the 10-Q).

recentDevelopments.headline: Steel River VPPA (Cypress Creek, Arkansas): 100% of initial output — 1.6 GW solar + ~2 GWh BESS phase 1, 2.5 GW/2.9 GWh full build
recentDevelopments.read: The largest US solar+storage PPA — and evidence that hyperscaler 24/7 goals have made BESS a core reliability asset in PPA structures. An LGES ~2.9 GWh supply role is reported but unconfirmed.

recentDevelopments.headline: $920M/month SpaceX-xAI compute deal: ~110,000 NVIDIA GPUs at xAI data centers, October 2026 through June 2029 (~$30B)
recentDevelopments.read: A frontier-lab competitor becomes a compute supplier — bridge capacity for Gemini Enterprise demand, with termination rights if GPUs slip past September 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: Intersect Power acquisition closed (~$4.75B): ~2.2 GW solar + 2.4 GWh BESS and the energy-park development model brought in-house
recentDevelopments.read: The first Big Tech acquisition of a major renewables developer — Google now competes with the developers other hyperscalers buy from; initial focus California and Texas solar+storage.

recentDevelopments.headline: Revealed as end user of the ~700 MW Hermantown, MN data center Mortenson's development arm is entitling
recentDevelopments.read: A new siting channel: hyperscale capacity originated by a GC's land-development arm, pending an updated environmental review.

recentDevelopments.headline: 1 GW of data-center demand response signed across five US utilities; ML workloads shift off-peak
recentDevelopments.read: Google is making flexible AI load a grid asset — demand response at this scale substitutes for peaker capacity and competes with (while also complementing) storage.

recentDevelopments.headline: Pine Island, MN data center powered via Xcel: 1,400 MW wind + 200 MW solar + 300 MW/30 GWh Form Energy iron-air battery — the largest battery project by energy capacity announced anywhere
recentDevelopments.read: Multi-day (100-hour) storage enters hyperscale procurement — a category-defining deal for LDES and a template (Google pays full costs via a dedicated tariff).

recentDevelopments.headline: WSJ reports Google exploring a ~USD 100M equity investment in Fluidstack tied to TPU distribution (reported, not confirmed by either party)
recentDevelopments.read: Would convert an arm's-length credit relationship into an ownership one and tie the backstop programme directly to TPU placement. Single-outlet reporting — treat as unconfirmed.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: revenue $402.8B, net income $132.2B; 2026 capex guided $175–185B (~doubling) — stock fell ~3% on the number
recentDevelopments.read: The original 2026 capex reset, since raised twice more — Alphabet 'reset the bar for AI infrastructure spending' (CNBC).

recentDevelopments.headline: Hut 8 River Bend: Google backstops the full 15-year, USD 7.0B base term with a springing Alphabet guarantee — and takes NO warrants and NO equity
recentDevelopments.read: The control case for the whole programme. Same service, same tenant, zero equity — so the 14% and 5.4% taken elsewhere were negotiated, not structural.

recentDevelopments.headline: NextEra co-development framework: gigawatt-scale data-center campuses, 15 GW of new generation by 2035 (30-35 GW upside) — after the October Duane Arnold 615 MW nuclear restart under a 25-year Google PPA
recentDevelopments.read: Google is buying generation development itself, not just PPAs — the deepest energy partnership any hyperscaler holds with an IPP.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cipher Barber Lake expansion: Google backstop increased by USD 333M to USD 1.73B as Fluidstack takes the whole 300 MW campus
recentDevelopments.read: Backstops are amended upward with the tenant's footprint — the instrument scales with the lease rather than being fixed at signing.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gemini 3 launched (Deep Think mode; 1501 LMArena Elo)
recentDevelopments.read: The model line whose demand pull Pichai credits for Cloud's acceleration — and the Siri win that followed extends it into Apple's installed base.

recentDevelopments.headline: $40B Texas commitment through 2027; 6,200+ MW of Texas PPAs including co-located solar+BESS at the Haskell County campus
recentDevelopments.read: The energy-park model at state scale — generation, storage, and data centers procured as one program.

recentDevelopments.headline: Abernathy, Texas: USD 1.3B of Google support behind the 168 MW TeraWulf-Fluidstack joint venture
recentDevelopments.read: Extends the programme from leases into a JV structure, and became the collateral story for USD 1.3B of 7.25% project notes two months later.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cipher Barber Lake: USD 1.4B Google backstop bought with penny warrants over 24,178,576 Cipher shares (~5.4% pro forma, USD 430.0M value floor)
recentDevelopments.read: Second landlord, second equity strip — and the first time the price of the backstop is disclosed with a floor, making the trade explicit rather than inferable.

recentDevelopments.headline: Search antitrust remedies: no Chrome divestiture, but exclusive-distribution bans (incl. Gemini) and mandated data-sharing; DOJ + 38 states cross-appealed (Feb 2026)
recentDevelopments.read: Better than the worst case, unresolved into 2027 — data-sharing remedies already bind while the appeal runs.

recentDevelopments.headline: TeraWulf backstops rise to $3.2B as Fluidstack's Lake Mariner leases expand — Google warrants reach ~14% of TeraWulf pro forma
recentDevelopments.read: Google is underwriting AI-buildout credit: downside protection via lease backstops, upside via penny warrants — ~$4.5B of support across the Fluidstack chain.

recentDevelopments.headline: Programme begins: Google signs the first per-building Recognition Agreements behind Fluidstack USA I's 200+ MW of Lake Mariner leases
recentDevelopments.read: The template for everything that follows — on a Fluidstack default or insolvency Google may pay the termination fee or assume the lease as tenant, which is what makes the landlords' project debt financeable.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Google has chosen ownership over procurement in energy: buying Intersect Power, co-developing energy parks, and anchoring first-of-kind storage (iron-air 30 GWh) and fusion offtakes make it the hyperscaler most likely to shape — rather than just consume — the storage market. Basis: closed acquisition, first-party project announcements.

(High confidence) We assess the TPU program has crossed from internal cost lever to competitive weapon: external sales, the Anthropic ~1M-TPU anchor, and Meta as a lessee give Google the only at-scale merchant alternative to NVIDIA among hyperscalers — with reported ambitions (~10% of NVIDIA-class revenue; 4.3M→35M unit projections) that remain analyst/reported figures, not guidance.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the interconnection queue is the strategic enemy Google is engineering around: energy parks (behind-the-meter generation+storage), 1 GW of demand response, and model tariff structures (Fort Wayne) all exist to add load without waiting for the grid — the playbook rivals will copy.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the sustainability gap is now structural: 66% hourly CFE but emissions +81% vs the 2019 baseline and 'moonshot getting harder' concessions — nuclear (nothing before ~2030) and fusion (early 2030s) cannot close it this decade, which keeps Google buying storage and renewables at maximum pace.

(Moderate confidence) We assess funding has shifted decisively to capital markets (~$95B of debt/equity raised across late 2025–2026) with FCF negative — sustainable at Alphabet's earnings power, but it makes the capex program hostage to equity-market patience in a way it wasn't in 2024.

(Low confidence) The Q2 2026 equity-gain composition (reported Anthropic/SpaceX marks; $37.7B vs $99B figures conflict across outlets) and Meta's reported outright TPU purchases from 2027 are unverified — treat both as unresolved.

The Fluidstack backstop programme is capacity procurement dressed as credit support. Google gets first call on gigawatts of AI capacity — at campuses whose end user is sometimes its own investee and whose silicon is sometimes its own TPU — without the leases, the land or the project debt appearing on Alphabet's balance sheet. The landlords get financeable paper; Google gets optionality it never had to capitalise.

The price of that support is negotiated, not structural — and Hut 8 proves it. Google took warrants over ~14% of TeraWulf and ~5.4% of Cipher, and nothing at all at Hut 8 for the same service on a larger lease. Any read that treats the equity strip as the standard cost of a Google backstop is wrong; the strip tracks the landlord's negotiating position, and the trend across the three deals runs downward.

relationships.note: Co-developing gigawatt-scale data-center campuses — 15 GW by 2035 base case — plus the Duane Arnold nuclear restart under a 25-year PPA.
relationships.context: December 2025: Google and NextEra agreed to co-develop gigawatt-scale campuses (first three in development; 15 GW of new generation for data-center hubs by 2035, 30-35 GW upside), with a technology leg putting Google Cloud AI into NextEra's grid software. It followed October's Duane Arnold deal — the 615 MW Iowa nuclear plant restarting Q1 2029 under a 25-year Google PPA. The deepest hyperscaler-IPP energy partnership on record.

relationships.note: $920M/month for ~110,000 NVIDIA GPUs at xAI data centers (Oct 2026 - Jun 2029, ~$30B).
relationships.context: Announced June 5, 2026: Google buys bridge capacity for Gemini Enterprise demand from SpaceX-xAI — ramp at reduced fees through September 2026, termination right if GPUs slip past end-September (one-month grace), and mutual 90-day cancellation after December 2026. A frontier-lab rival as compute landlord — the starkest sign that capacity scarcity outranks competitive hygiene.

relationships.note: ~USD 4.5B of credit backstops across the Fluidstack-TeraWulf lease chain, bought with penny warrants now ~14% of TeraWulf — the first and largest instrument in the programme.
relationships.context:
Google provides amortising lease backstops behind Fluidstack's TeraWulf capacity — USD 3.2bn across the Lake Mariner leases and USD 1.3bn at the Abernathy joint venture — under per-building Recognition Agreements that oblige Google, on a Fluidstack payment default or insolvency event, either to pay the termination fee or to pay all rent currently due and assume the lease as tenant. It took warrants over 32,568,197 TeraWulf shares, about 14% pro forma.

The backstop switches on at lease commencement rather than at signing: TeraWulf's Q2 2026 10-Q records USD 600m of it becoming effective when CB-3 was delivered. TeraWulf's own FY2025 10-K says the Google credit support 'was a key factor in enabling efficient financing and phased development' — which is the point of the instrument. This pair is knowingly recorded as `partner` here and `investor` from TeraWulf's side, and is on the relationships-checker accept list: both are true at once.

relationships.note: GC of the ~$2B Fort Wayne campus and the New Albany 'Mustang Project'.
relationships.context: Holder is the confirmed GC of Google's ~$2B, 700+ acre Fort Wayne, Indiana data center (ground broken April 2024) and holds the OSHA-documented 'Mustang Project' in New Albany, Ohio — the low-profile incumbent of Google's hyperscale build program, with 60-70% of its projects in data centers.

relationships.note: End user of the ~700 MW Hermantown, MN site Mortenson Properties is entitling.
relationships.context: March 2026: the city of Hermantown revealed Google as end user of the ~700 MW data center Mortenson's development arm is entitling — hyperscale capacity originated through a GC's land-development channel, pending an updated environmental review with the MCEA lawsuit on hold.

relationships.note: Honeysuckle solar (188 MW, Indiana) contracted — 'supporting Google's Fort Wayne data center campus'.
relationships.context: Lightsource bp's Honeysuckle project delivers 188 MW of Indiana solar under a Google offtake explicitly framed as supporting the Fort Wayne data-center campus — PPA-mediated energy supply attached to the same campus Holder builds.

relationships.note: Reuters-reported capacity supply to Google Cloud — never company-confirmed.
relationships.context: June 2025 Reuters reporting had CoreWeave providing compute capacity to Google Cloud (which in turn supplies OpenAI); earlier reports had Google in talks to rent Blackwell GPUs. Neither company has confirmed — held as reported-only.

relationships.note: Reported Google Cloud compute supply to OpenAI after exclusivity ended — terms unconfirmed; also the defining model rival.
relationships.context: Reuters reported (June 2025) OpenAI adding Google Cloud as a compute provider, and the April 2026 Microsoft restructuring formally freed OpenAI to buy Google capacity — no primary announcement or terms. Simultaneously Gemini's chief rival: supplier economics and existential competition in one relationship.

relationships.note: Zacks reports Flex has secured substantial incremental business from hyperscaler and data-centre customers including Google, with those projects moving into the capital deployment phase.
relationships.context:
Curated on a single third-party source that names the counterparty explicitly, and flagged as such rather than presented as firmly established.

Flex itself has never named Google as a customer. Its own material mentions Google only in a sentence listing hyperscalers as participants in the data-centre market, which is commentary and not a customer statement — and Flex's annual report discloses that its ten largest customers were 45% of FY2026 net sales while naming none of them.

The link carries less weight than Flex's Amazon relationship, which rests on a filed warrant agreement. It should not be read as establishing the unnamed customer that reached 12% of Flex's net sales in the quarter ended June 2026.

relationships.via: Xcel Energy Electric Service Agreement and Clean Energy Accelerator Charge
relationships.note: Form Energy supplies the 300 MW / 30 GWh iron-air battery serving Google's Pine Island data centre through Xcel Energy's tariff.
relationships.context:
The largest battery project by energy capacity announced anywhere, and Google pays for it: all costs of the new service and any new grid infrastructure sit with Google under a Clean Energy Accelerator Charge modelled on the Clean Transition Tariff it developed with NV Energy, plus $50m into Xcel's Capacity*Connect programme. TechCrunch, citing The Information, reported the price to Form as about $1bn — roughly $33 per kilowatt-hour — while Canary Media called it undisclosed and Xcel's release does not state it.

One characterisation to avoid, because several outlets use it: Google is not an investor in Form Energy. No Alphabet, GV or CapitalG entity appears in any Form funding round from Series A through the August 2026 Series G, on Form's investor wall, or in the investor list Form filed to ISO New England. Headlines describing Google as 'backing' Form, or as having 'invested $1 billion', are loose language for this offtake. The Electric Service Agreement remains pending before the Minnesota commission in docket E002/M-26-170.

relationships.note: The tenant Google's whole lease-backstop programme stands behind — Fluidstack is the lessee of record at every campus, and Google has never published a page naming it.
relationships.context:
Fluidstack Ltd is the counterparty at the centre of the programme: it signs the lease with the landlord, and Google signs a Recognition Agreement per building promising to step in on a Fluidstack payment default or insolvency event. Disclosed support runs to roughly USD 3.2bn at TeraWulf's Lake Mariner, USD 1.3bn at the Abernathy joint venture, USD 1.73bn at Cipher's Barber Lake (USD 1.4bn at signing plus a USD 333m increase) and the full fifteen-year base term at Hut 8's River Bend, plus a master lease at New Lebanon, Indiana.

The relationship is almost entirely one-directional in public: the mechanics live in the LANDLORDS' 8-Ks, Fluidstack's single joint release calls Google 'a leading global hyperscale partner', and Google has published nothing naming Fluidstack. The Wall Street Journal reported in February 2026 that Google was exploring a ~USD 100m equity investment tied to TPU distribution. Fluidstack itself has raised repeatedly through 2026 and Forbes put it at an USD 18bn valuation in September 2026, explicitly on the strength of building Google's and Anthropic's data centres.

relationships.note: Backstops the full 15-year, USD 7.0bn River Bend base term — and took NO warrants and NO equity, unlike at TeraWulf and Cipher.
relationships.context:
Hut 8's River Bend campus in West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana is 245 MW of critical IT on 330 MW of Entergy capacity, leased to a Fluidstack subsidiary on a 15-year triple-net lease worth USD 7.0bn over the base term. Google backstops the rent and related pass-through obligations, with a springing Alphabet Inc. guarantee if Google's revenue falls below 50% of consolidated Alphabet revenue.

What distinguishes this instrument from every other one in the programme is its price: Google took no warrants and no equity in Hut 8, where it took about 14% of TeraWulf and about 5.4% of Cipher for the same service. No source located explains the difference. It is the single most useful comparison point in the programme, because it shows the equity component is negotiated rather than structural.

relationships.note: Backstops USD 1.73bn of Fluidstack's Barber Lake rent and holds penny warrants over ~5.4% of Cipher — the coherent inverse of Cipher's `investor` is `portfolio`, which the enum does not carry.
relationships.context:
Cipher Digital Inc. (renamed from Cipher Mining in February 2026) is Fluidstack's landlord at Barber Lake, Mitchell County, Texas: 300 MW gross / 207 MW critical IT on a ten-year modified-gross lease worth about USD 3.8bn over the initial term. Google backstops USD 1.73bn of Fluidstack's obligations there — USD 1.4bn at signing in September 2025 plus a USD 333m increase in November — and took warrants over 24,178,576 Cipher shares at USD 0.01, about 5.4% pro forma, with a USD 430.0m value floor.

Cipher's Q2 2026 10-Q carries a USD 544.5m asset for 'the value of Google agreeing to make the lease payments from Fluidstack', and the amortisation of Cipher's USD 1,733m of 7.125% project notes tracks the Google backstop rather than a fixed schedule — so the credit support is measured, capitalised and structurally load-bearing on the landlord's balance sheet. Cipher correctly types Google `investor`; the schema's `type` enum has no `portfolio`, so this side is typed `other` and the pair is accepted, exactly as for `amazon x mainspring-energy` and the three MGX pairs.

relationships.note: Buys TPUs at gigawatt scale ('up to one million') and is the end user at River Bend, the campus Google's own backstop underwrites.
relationships.context:
Anthropic is Google's largest external TPU customer — 'up to one million' chips, with 'well over a gigawatt' of capacity in 2026 — and Alphabet is also an Anthropic shareholder. The two strands meet at River Bend: Anthropic is the end user of the Hut 8 campus that Fluidstack leases and Google backstops, under the AI infrastructure partnership Hut 8, Anthropic and Fluidstack announced on 17 December 2025.

That makes the backstop programme legible as something more than credit support: Google is underwriting the rent of a campus that runs its own silicon for its own investee. Anthropic types Google `supplier`; this side is the coherent inverse.
relationships.via: TPU supply; River Bend end user

policyExposure.exposure: The September 2025 search-antitrust remedies bar exclusive distribution deals (Gemini included) and mandate data-sharing, though Chrome was not divested; the DOJ and 38 states cross-appealed (February 2026, argued late 2026/early 2027), and the data-sharing remedies already bind while the appeal runs. The dossier reads the Apple-Siri Gemini win as exactly the distribution the remedies were designed to constrain — better than the worst case, but unresolved into 2027.

specs.label: Effective date
specs.value: At lease commencement, not at signing — TeraWulf recorded USD 600m switching on when CB-3 was delivered

specs.label: Lake Mariner, NY
specs.value: ~USD 3.2bn behind Fluidstack USA I's 378 MW of critical IT

specs.label: Abernathy, TX
specs.value: USD 1.3bn behind the 168 MW joint venture

specs.label: Barber Lake, TX
specs.value: USD 1.73bn (USD 1.4bn at signing + USD 333m increase) behind Fluidstack USA II's 300 MW gross / 207 MW critical IT

specs.label: River Bend, LA
specs.value: Full 15-year base term of a USD 7.0bn lease, 245 MW critical IT, with a springing Alphabet Inc. guarantee if Google's revenue falls below 50% of consolidated Alphabet revenue

specs.label: New Lebanon, IN
specs.value: Master lease — the least-documented instrument in the set

specs.label: TeraWulf
specs.value: Penny warrants over 32,568,197 shares, ~14% pro forma

specs.label: Cipher
specs.value: Penny warrants over 24,178,576 shares at USD 0.01, ~5.4% pro forma, USD 430.0m value floor

specs.label: Hut 8
specs.value: NOTHING — no warrants and no equity, for the same service

specs.label: Measured as an asset
specs.value: Cipher's Q2 2026 10-Q carries USD 544.5m for 'the value of Google agreeing to make the lease payments from Fluidstack'; its USD 1,733m of 7.125% project notes amortise against the backstop rather than a fixed schedule

technicalSpecs.notes: Assembled from the LANDLORDS' filings. Google publishes nothing naming Fluidstack, and no source publishes a programme-level total — the per-instrument figures above are the whole disclosed record. 'Full base term' at River Bend is a description, not a dollar cap, so the components are not summable into a single exposure number.

periods.commentary: Third capex raise of 2026; ~$49.6B equity/convertible + $20.3B notes raised; 2027 capex guided to 'significantly increase' again.
FY2024 for reference: revenue $350.0B, EPS $8.04, capex $52.5B; the Feb 2025 '$75B' guide was the cycle's first Alphabet capex shock.

financials.commentary: Antitrust: search remedies (Sept 2025) bar exclusive distribution and mandate data-sharing; no Chrome divestiture; DOJ/38-state cross-appeal argued late 2026/early 2027. EU cumulative fines >€8B incl. €2.95B adtech (Sept 2025). Sustainability: 66% hourly CFE; total footprint +18% in 2025, +81% vs 2019.
